summary_responses.response: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has proposed a new Privacy Act system of records, Treasury .033, to support its oversight and management of the federal student aid portfolio under an interagency agreement with the Department of Education. summary_responses.response: Microservice architectures can experience temporary overload when independently managed services scale out of sync, rejecting valuable transactions and allowing attackers to cause damage with floods of cheap, low-priority requests. Conventional retries fail to protect important traffic during overload and can worsen congestion through retry storms, wasted resources, and unnecessary scaling. The paper proposes DiffTry, a lightweight, distributed, stateless mechanism that assigns class-specific retry budgets—giving high-priority requests more attempts and low-priority requests fewer—without requiring overload detection or coordination between services. The authors develop analytical models for individual services and general service networks to estimate rejection and throughput rates, and they derive guarantees supporting DiffTry’s effectiveness against both incidental and adversarial overloads. Simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment using a drop-in service-mesh plugin, requiring no application changes, closely match the analysis and demonstrate network-wide prioritization.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is issuing a direct final rule updating its title 5 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to codify statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023 and previously implemented through policy guidance. Effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, the rule makes virtually all Federal civilian service—including temporary or intermittent service—count toward the 12-month qualifying-service requirement, although employees must still independently qualify as covered employees to use title 5 FMLA leave. It also allows honorable active service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps, alone or combined with qualifying civilian service, to satisfy that requirement, but not Coast Guard or Public Health Service commissioned-corps service. The rule additionally excludes Veterans Health Administration employees covered by a separate leave system from title 5 FMLA coverage and confirms that annual or sick leave provided under an authority outside title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. Because paid parental leave is substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, these eligibility changes also affect paid parental leave for qualifying employees following a child’s birth or placement for adoption or foster care.
